instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: A wildfire is an uncontrolled fire which spreads through large amounts of vegetation. It is unpredictable and very dangerous. They can start naturally, for example due to lightning strikes, or they can start due to human behaviour, for example from campfires. In Canada, it is believed that roughly half of all wildfires are started by lightning.
atoms.sound: A wildfire is an uncontrolled fire which spreads through large amounts of vegetation. It is unpredictable and very dangerous. They can start naturally, for example due to lightning strikes, or they can start due to human behaviour, for example from campfires. In Canada, it is believed that roughly half of all wildfires are started by lightning.

atoms.text: Wildfires damage the environment because they release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Wildfires also drive wildlife out of their natural habitat, which damages biodiversity. In July 2023, Canadian wildfires burnt 59000 square miles of land.
atoms.sound: Wildfires damage the environment because they release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Wildfires also drive wildlife out of their natural habitat, which damages biodiversity. In July 2023, Canadian wildfires burnt fifty-nine thousand square miles of land.

atoms.text: Another danger for humans and animals is smoke produced by the fire. Winds blew the smoke from the Canadian forests down to New York, where the sky became filled with thick orange smoke. Inhaling this smoke can cause problems with breathing and increase the risk of heart attacks and lung cancer.
